question: Which month had the highest sales?

criteria.text: Names {best_month} as the best month (about {best_month_net} after cancellations, or {best_month_sales} before).

question: Which month had the lowest sales?

criteria.text: Doesn't present {partial_month} as the weakest month without saying it's incomplete: the data ends on {last_day}.
Names the weakest full month as {weakest_full_net} (after subtracting cancellations) or {weakest_full_sales} (before), and the answer makes clear which it means if that matters.

question: Which day of the week brings in the most sales, and how does Saturday compare?

criteria.text: Names {best_weekday} as the day with the most sales.
Says there are no Saturday sales in the data at all (the file has {saturday_rows} Saturday rows), rather than giving Saturday a figure or ranking it.

question: Which country outside the UK brings in the most revenue?

criteria.text: Names the {top_country} (about {top_country_revenue}).

question: What share of revenue comes from the UK?

criteria.text: Gives about {uk_share} (anything from {uk_share_lo} to {uk_share_hi} counts).

question: Which product sold the most units?

criteria.text: Names the top product and makes clear how products are grouped. Grouping by product name, it's {top_units_product} (about {top_units} units after cancellations, or {top_units_gross} before). Grouping by stock code, it's {top_units_code_product} (about {top_units_code} units), because that code is sold under two names. Either counts.
Doesn't name {trap_units_product} as the top seller. Its {trap_units} units were a single order that was cancelled the same day.

question: Which product brought in the most revenue?

criteria.text: Names {top_revenue_product} (about {top_revenue} after cancellations, or {top_revenue_gross} before).
Doesn't present DOTCOM POSTAGE ({postage_revenue}) as the top product. It's a postage charge, not a product; mentioning it as a non-product line is fine.

question: What share of customers ordered more than once?

criteria.text: Gives about {repeat_share} of customers with a customer ID (anything from {repeat_lo} to {repeat_hi} counts), counting distinct orders that weren't cancelled.

question: What was the shop's total revenue over the whole period?

criteria.text: Reports revenue after cancellations of about {total_net} (anything from {total_lo} to {total_hi} counts), or gross sales of about {total_gross} with cancellations of about {cancelled_value} stated separately. Gross sales alone, as if nothing was cancelled, doesn't count.

question: How many customers does the shop have?

criteria.text: Gives about {customers} customers who bought something ({customers_any} if it also counts customers who only cancelled).
Says that about {missing_id_share} of rows have no customer ID, so the real number of customers is likely higher.

Gives an average per order (adding up each invoice's lines, leaving out cancellations) between {aov_lo} and {aov_hi}: about {aov} over all orders, or {aov_with_id} counting only orders with a customer ID. A clearly labelled median of about {aov_median} also counts. The average per line item, about {line_value}, doesn't.
Gives about {cancelled_orders} cancelled orders (invoices starting with "C"), about {cancelled_share} of all invoices. Counting the {cancelled_lines} cancelled line items as orders doesn't count.

question: Before I use this data, are there any quality problems I should know about?

criteria.text: Mentions cancelled orders or negative quantities.
Mentions rows with no customer ID (about {missing_id_share}).
Mentions duplicate rows (there are {duplicates}).
Mentions lines that aren't products, such as postage, fees, discounts or manual adjustments.
Mentions zero or negative prices ({zero_price_lines} lines).

question: What's our profit margin on the Regency cakestand?

criteria.text: Says the data has no cost information, so the profit margin can't be calculated from it.
Doesn't present a profit margin as if it came from the data. Clearly labelled hypothetical assumptions are fine.
Says the data has no visitor or traffic information, so the conversion rate can't be calculated from it.
Doesn't give a conversion rate as if it came from the data.
